title: Palace urges Lacson to file charges on flood control double funds
summary: Malacañang urged Sen. Panfilo Lacson to file charges on alleged duplicate appropriations for some flood control projects and multipurpose buildings in the proposed 2027 national budget.

blocks.text: Malacañang on Tuesday urged Senator Panfilo Lacson to file charges on the alleged duplicate appropriations for some flood control projects and multipurpose buildings in the proposed 2027 national budget.

"Kung may nakita na po si Senator Lacson na naging ghost project sa sinasabi niyo ng mga multipurpose buildings, umpisahan na po nating sampahan ng kaso," Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said in a press briefing.
(If Senator Lacson has already found any ghost projects among the multipurpose buildings he is referring to, start filing cases against them.)
"May mga verified documents po siyang pinanghahawakan para masimulan ang pagsampahan ng kaso," she added.
(Lacson has verified documents to start filing the charges.)
GMA News Online has reached out to Lacson for comment on the matter.
Castro said a thorough investigation is needed since not all repeated appropriations are double appropriations since some projects are funded by phase.
"Since ito ay suspected ghost projects, mas mabuting ipagbigay alam ni rin ni Sen Lascon sa DPWH ang mga maaring anomalya," she said.
(Since these are suspected ghost projects, it is better for Lacson to inform the Department of Public Works and Highways of the possibly anomalies.)
Castro said President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. would veto the proposed 2027 budget should any anomaly be found.
Lacson earlier criticized P241 billion worth of fragmented assistance programs in the Senate version of the proposed 2027 national budget.

Lacson said the Senate should reconsider the allocations, arguing that the P241 billion in "fragmented" aid programs and funding for thousands of multipurpose buildings would not address the country's economic concerns.
The senator also flagged duplicate appropriations for some flood control projects.
“We found more irregularities. Double appropriations. Not only are these flood control projects, but they have also been allocated funding twice,” he said. — BM, GMA News
